newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds finish flat ahead of Congress vote.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds finish flat ahead of Congress vote.

text.p: Argentine bonds finished flat to slightly higher Wednesday after a strong opening ended in small changes in prices from Tuesday's close.

"It was a different day with more of the same," said a trader at a large Argentine bank, referring to the market's inability to make headway until the government's tax-hiking measures to plug the budget deficit are finally passed. The market was unchanged on Tuesday as well.
After weeks of waiting, Congress began discussing the measures Wednesday. That is still no guarantee that the whole plan will be passed, but at least the wheels are in motion, traders said.
The 5.5 percent dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 rose $0.07 to 117.42, after rising as high as 118.0 in the morning. Argentina's FRB due 2005 rose 1/2 to 81.

Traders said the local market was boosted in the morning by short-covering in New York for Argentine FRBs. That buying resulted from demand for Latin American paper emanating from rising hopes Brazil's Senate will pass Thursday a bill authorizing the Central Bank to buy back Brady bonds and swap them for other sovereign debt, said an analyst.
But in the afternoon, the market was pulled back down by some profit-taking by local funds, said traders.
Market players reported that Thursday's session will depend on the outcome of the congressional debate on the government measures. The debate is expected to last through the night.
In the money markets, one-day call money rates fell to 7.15 percent from 7.30 percent.
